The frequency column of r1 holds for every device (same L and law); devices with more output charge need a larger reverse current (I_zvs) to swing the node in 300 ns, which makes the ripple and the RMS current larger. Conduction dominates everything but the IGBT; the IGBT's turn-off tail is r1's.

## 2. Forced hard commutation (480 V raw; the high side turns on while the low side's reverse path carries I)

Loop inductance between the bridge's 100 nF and the switch: 20 / 40 nH. Generic model (est.): turning-on switch as a resistance falling to R_on over the datasheet's rise time; the freewheeling device as Co(tr) plus a charge-control diode holding the datasheet's Qrr (snappy: pessimistic for the overshoot; the SiC cascode's datasheet Qrr 73 nC and the SiC MOSFET's Qfr 34 nC include their output charge, which is already the Co(tr) here, so 5 / 2 nC of true recovery charge are used); no RC snubber except the SiC cascode's required 5 ohm + 100 pF. The IGBT is M15's calibrated case. Energy per event in the turning-on device; 'every cycle' = that energy x f added to its TCM loss.

Reading: with a reverse path that has (almost) no recovered charge (both cascodes, e-mode GaN, SiC MOSFET) a forced hard turn-on costs the Coss charge of both devices times the rail plus the overlap: 10-40 uJ at 0.8-2.5 A, repeated every cycle 0.5-6 W: survivable for a second on the chassis, and every datasheet among them shows the device hard-switched (the cascode GaN 'in both hard- and soft-switched circuits'). The superjunction part dumps Qrr x V (0.4-0.8 uC typ / max at only 100 A/us) plus its huge Co(tr): 200-400 uJ per event, 10-60 W every cycle, and its body diode is rated to 70 V/ns: this is the failure mode the user means; it is out. The overshoot is set by the hard edge's rate against the loop inductance: at the datasheets' fastest rise times (5 ns) the SiC MOSFET and the e-mode GaN ring to 700-880 V with 20-40 nH, above 650 V (and the e-mode GaN's 750 V < 1 us transient rating); slowed to a 20 ns turn-on (gate resistor) they stay near 500-560 V. The cascode GaN as the maker tests it (RG 70 ohm + 240 ohm bead: 50-65 V/ns) peaks at 490-530 V, with 800 V transient rating behind it; the SiC cascode with its required RC snubber at 590-680 V, but it is the one part with an avalanche rating (33 mJ).

## 3. Gate margin, chassis tab, gate supply

Spurious turn-on: the off device's gate rises by C_rss / C_iss x dV (charge division, no driver help) or by R_sink x C_rss x dv/dt (driver holding the gate through about 2 ohm): TCM edges 4 V/ns, a forced hard edge at the device's own dv/dt (section 2). Tab: TO-220 on the 2 mm plate through a 1.5 mm Al2O3 washer (about 7 pF, 1 K/W) or a 0.23 mm silicone pad (about 21 pF, 0.5-1 K/W); common-mode current = C x dv/dt.

In every TO-220 half-bridge one tab is the switch node: the low side's for drain / collector-tab parts, the high side's for the source-tab cascode GaN (its low side then has a quiet tab at the shunt, i.e. ground). Budget: 25 mA.

## 4. Fixed-frequency hard switching (no TCM) with the cascode GaN / SiC

L1 470 uH, fixed f, both edges as they fall: the high side's turn-on is hard whenever the valley current is positive (about Qoss x V + Eoss + overlap; est.), the other edges soft. Same output filter as recommended (its first resonance moves to 0.65 kHz with 470 uH); residue at the power amp from r2's model.

Hard switching costs the Coss charge at every period where the valley stays positive (400 V region): with the cascode GaN about 1.5-2.2 W at 100-150 kHz at full load, against 0.3 W in TCM; at 150-250 V the 470 uH ripple reverses the current by itself and the bridge is soft anyway. The edge rate of a hard edge (30-100 V/ns) puts 0.2-2 A common-mode spikes through the switch-node tab's capacitance, against 30-80 mA in TCM.
